reason: The text contains explicit divine instructions for sacrifice and worship. Exodus 20:24-26 specifies: 'An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shall sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings.' The covenant ceremony in Exodus 24 demonstrates sacrifices as central to the covenant-making process. Furthermore, the golden calf incident (Exodus 32) illustrates what constitutes IMPROPER worship—the people perform sacrifices to an idol—which implicitly affirms that proper worship (monotheistic, directed to Yahweh alone) is what matters to God. While the passage also emphasizes obedience and covenant-keeping, the text clearly establishes that proper worship and sacrifice are indeed important to Yahweh.
